title: Ship multi-architecture cluster and appliance packages
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Ship multi-architecture cluster and appliance packages
events.body:
## Outcome

Run the same headless node reproducibly on common server, ARM single-board, clustered, and network-storage appliance environments.

## Implementation

- Publish rootless x86-64 and ARM64 OCI images from one source revision and attach per-architecture digests.
- Provide declarative clustered deployment manifests with persistent volumes, disruption behavior, ingress choices, resource limits, and rolling upgrade checks.
- Package an unprivileged network-storage appliance bundle with explicit share permissions and service lifecycle commands.
- Add encrypted identity export and import, backup and restore, health, metrics, and a compact monitoring view across every package.
- Test graceful upgrade, rollback, node replacement, and data portability between architecture and package types.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each clean-install fixture starts, becomes healthy, serves a verified clone, reports metrics, backs up, restores, and stops cleanly.
- Images and bundles do not require privileged execution or host-wide mounts.
- Identity export is encrypted and never prints key material.
- Moving durable data between supported architectures preserves repository and identity verification.
- A failed rolling upgrade leaves a healthy serving replica and supports rollback.

## Dependencies

Builds on the service contract in #442 and rootless image in #456; deployment roles are wired in #457.

## Verification

Build both architectures, validate manifests, run appliance and clustered clean installs, clone, inspect health and metrics, export and import identity, back up and restore, replace a node, upgrade, fail, roll back, and scan permissions.
